sections.title: About Ben Harkness
sections.html:
Ben brings 28 years of information technology leadership experience, including 26 years with Utah Cancer Specialists. Before joining UCS, he worked as part of a regional IT team with CommonSpirit Health. His professional certifications include MCSE, CompTIA A+, CNE, and CCSA.

Although Ben was initially hesitant about making the move into healthcare, his experience at UCS quickly changed his perspective. Working alongside physicians who are genuinely compassionate and deeply committed to their patients has given his work a greater sense of purpose. He values being part of an organization where technology and infrastructure ultimately support the people providing care.

Ben is especially encouraged by UCS’s growing focus on the patient experience. He is excited to see the organization continue looking at its services, systems, and decisions through the eyes of the patient and finding new ways to make their experience better.

For Ben, exceptional care begins with truly knowing the patient and understanding what they need. He believes that the better we understand each individual, the better equipped we are to provide the care, support, and experience that are right for them.

Outside of work, Ben is happiest outdoors. He enjoys exploring Jeep trails throughout Southern Utah, hiking and skiing in the nearby mountains, and traveling to experience different parts of the world. He also enjoys golfing with his daughters, tackling challenging Jeep trails, and building, repairing, and flying radio-controlled aircraft.

sections.title: About DeAnn Angilau
sections.html:
DeAnn Angilau is a Registered Nurse and Oncology Certified Nurse (OCN®) with more than 30 years of experience in oncology nursing, clinical operations, and healthcare leadership. She currently serves as Director of Clinical Services at Utah Cancer Specialists, where she oversees multi-site clinical operations, multidisciplinary teams, nurse navigation, quality and safety initiatives, and value-based care programs.

DeAnn joined Utah Cancer Specialists in 1992 and has grown alongside the organization, beginning in direct patient care and advancing into leadership. Her extensive frontline oncology experience continues to shape her approach to clinical operations, staff education, program development, and patient care.

She was drawn to healthcare by a desire to support people during some of the most difficult and vulnerable moments of their lives. Early in her nursing career, she discovered a passion for oncology and for the meaningful relationships that develop with patients and their families throughout the cancer journey. She has remained with UCS because of its commitment to providing high-quality, compassionate care and the opportunity to continually improve how patients are supported.

Looking ahead, DeAnn is excited about the continued growth of Utah Cancer Specialists and the opportunity to develop innovative ways to provide exceptional, patient-centered care. She is especially passionate about expanding care coordination, navigation, supportive services, and value-based care programs that support patients throughout every stage of their cancer journey.

For DeAnn, exceptional patient care begins with treating each patient as a person, not simply a diagnosis. She believes every patient has a unique story, needs, and concerns and deserves to feel seen, heard, and supported. Her philosophy is simple: provide safe, high-quality, compassionate care and treat every patient the way she would want her own family to be treated.

Outside of work, DeAnn’s favorite place to be is with her family, especially her grandchildren. She enjoys family game nights, cheering on her grandkids at sporting events, and spending time with the youngest members of the family. She is also a big college football and basketball fan, enjoys Christian music, and considers anywhere with a beach, a beautiful sunset, and warm, sunny weather her happy place.

sections.title: About Johnny Walker
sections.html:
Johnny has more than 25 years of experience in clinical research and has spent nearly 20 years serving as Director of Clinical Research at Utah Cancer Specialists. Throughout his career, he has been committed to expanding access to innovative treatment options and ensuring patients have opportunities to participate in meaningful clinical trials close to home.

Early in his research career, Johnny authored a paper examining genetic differences in warfarin metabolism and had the opportunity to present his work at the American College of Cardiology. He later joined Utah Cancer Specialists, where he was given the opportunity to lead and grow the organization’s clinical research program in an increasingly complex and rapidly evolving field.

What continues to excite Johnny most about clinical research is the expansion of new therapies and treatment approaches available to patients. He values the role research can play in providing additional options and advancing cancer care for both current and future patients.

Johnny’s focus is on bringing high-quality clinical trials to Utah Cancer Specialists while also considering the practical impact participation may have on patients and their families. He works closely with physicians, research staff, sponsors, and partners to identify trials that offer meaningful opportunities while minimizing unnecessary financial burden whenever possible.

Outside of work, Johnny enjoys spending time outdoors, particularly fishing, hunting, and camping.

sections.title: About Kyle Kitchen
sections.html:
Kyle Kitchen brings more than 25 years of pharmacy and healthcare leadership experience to Utah Cancer Specialists. He earned his Doctor of Pharmacy from the University of Utah and later completed his MBA at Weber State University. Before joining UCS, Kyle spent 19 years with Intermountain Health in a variety of pharmacy leadership roles. He has now been with Utah Cancer Specialists for nearly eight years.

Kyle was drawn to healthcare by a desire to help others live healthier, happier lives. Joining Utah Cancer Specialists offered an opportunity to take his career in a new direction, and he has valued the chance to be part of an organization so focused on advancing cancer care.

One of the things he appreciates most about UCS is the commitment of its physicians and staff to bringing new and advanced therapies to patients. He has seen tremendous growth in treatment options and is proud to work alongside teams dedicated to making those therapies available to as many patients as possible.

Kyle believes strongly in partnering with patients and their care teams to improve care in ways that are most meaningful to each individual. For him, the best healthcare decisions are those that combine clinical expertise with an understanding of what matters most to the patient.

Outside of work, Kyle enjoys spending time outdoors, traveling, and working in the yard.

sections.title: About Mark Williams
sections.html:
With a background in healthcare finance, accounting, and operations, Mark brings experience in financial reporting, budgeting and forecasting, cash-flow management, process improvement, contracts, and organizational growth. At Utah Cancer Specialists, he focuses on turning complex financial information into practical insights that support thoughtful decision-making and the long-term strength of the organization. He is also passionate about developing people, improving systems, and helping teams understand how their work contributes to UCS’s mission.

He holds a Master of Business Administration and a bachelor’s degree in marketing management and continues to pursue professional development in healthcare finance, accounting, and leadership.

He was drawn to healthcare because of the meaningful impact it has on patients and families. While his role primarily takes place behind the scenes, he believes strong financial stewardship plays an important part in exceptional patient care by ensuring physicians and staff have the resources, people, and systems they need to do their best work. He was especially drawn to Utah Cancer Specialists because of its patient-centered approach, strong community roots, and commitment to growing while remaining focused on the people it serves.

Looking ahead, he is excited about UCS’s continued growth and the opportunity to bring high-quality cancer care to more patients and communities. He believes that strengthening systems, using information effectively, and planning thoughtfully for the future will help UCS continue serving patients and families for generations.

Outside of work, he enjoys spending time with his wife and three children, writing, teaching, exploring new technology, and working on hands-on projects. Writing is one of his favorite creative outlets, particularly developing books and resources that make complicated topics more practical and approachable.

For him, exceptional patient care means seeing each patient as a person—not simply a diagnosis. It means providing compassionate, timely, and clinically excellent care while reducing unnecessary financial and administrative burdens. His goal is to provide strong stewardship behind the scenes that allows UCS physicians and staff to remain focused on what matters most: caring for patients.

sections.title: About Rachelle Tonga
sections.html:
Rachelle Tonga brings more than 25 years of leadership experience with Utah Cancer Specialists, along with a deep understanding of oncology practice operations, employee development, and patient-centered care. She began her career with UCS as a Patient Service Representative and has advanced through a variety of leadership roles, including Office Manager, Associate Director and Company Trainer, and ultimately Director.

Throughout her tenure, Rachelle has had the opportunity to grow alongside UCS and witness its evolution into one of Utah’s leading community oncology practices. She has played an important role in mentoring, training, and developing staff members and leaders across the organization. Prior to joining UCS, Rachelle spent seven years as an Office Manager for a gynecologic oncology practice at LDS Hospital.

Rachelle was drawn to healthcare because of her genuine interest in people and her desire to support others during some of life’s most difficult moments. She values the relationships she has built with both patients and employees and believes that compassion, empathy, and personal connection are essential to creating an exceptional healthcare experience.

As UCS continues to grow, Rachelle is excited about the advancements in cancer treatment, technology, and personalized care that will further improve the patient experience. She is equally passionate about building a workplace where employees feel valued, supported, and connected to the organization’s purpose. For Rachelle, maintaining the human touch that has always defined UCS is just as important as embracing innovation and growth.

To Rachelle, exceptional patient care means truly listening, understanding what each patient needs, and ensuring they feel heard, respected, and supported throughout their care. She believes every interaction matters, particularly in oncology, where kindness, understanding, and exceptional service can make a meaningful difference for patients and their families.

Outside of work, Rachelle enjoys traveling, reading, crafting, photography, and spending time outdoors. Most of all, she treasures time with her family and grandchildren and loves hosting gatherings that bring the people she cares about together and create lasting memories.

sections.title: About Ravin Bisla
sections.html:
Ravin Bisla earned a Bachelor of Science in Economics from Duke University and an MBA in Finance from the UCLA Anderson School of Management. With both of his parents working as physicians, medicine and the importance of putting patients first were part of his life from an early age and continue to shape the way he approaches healthcare leadership today.

Ravin is a strong believer in the value of community oncology and the difference it can make for patients and families. As healthcare has become increasingly complex and consolidated, he believes organizations like Utah Cancer Specialists offer something especially important: high-quality, specialized care delivered with greater accessibility, personal attention, and a focus on the individual rather than the system.

In his leadership, Ravin works to ensure that the organization never loses sight of what patients may be experiencing. What can feel like a routine day of work for a healthcare team may coincide with one of the most difficult chapters in a patient’s life. That perspective drives his commitment to going above and beyond, both clinically and personally, for patients and their families.

Outside of work, Ravin enjoys spending time outdoors, especially skiing, hiking, camping, off-roading, and shooting. He is happiest in the mountains.

sections.title: About Sandy Jones
sections.html:
Sandy Jones is an accomplished healthcare marketing leader with experience in brand strategy, organizational growth, communications, culture, and patient engagement. As Director of Marketing for Utah Cancer Specialists, she leads initiatives focused on strengthening the organization’s brand, expanding community relationships, supporting growth, and creating a more connected experience for patients, providers, and employees.

Sandy’s leadership approach is centered on people. She believes the strongest organizations are built from the inside out—through engaged teams, trusted relationships, clear communication, and a genuine understanding of the people they serve. She is passionate about making healthcare more approachable and ensuring that an organization’s brand reflects the quality, expertise, and compassion patients experience firsthand.

She is a Certified High Performance Coach through the High Performance Institute and a certified facilitator of FranklinCovey leadership programs. Her training includes Multipliers®, The 4 Essential Roles of Leadership, The Speed of Trust, and The 6 Critical Practices for Leading a Team, reflecting her ongoing commitment to developing strong leaders and high-performing teams.

Service has also been an important part of Sandy’s life and leadership. She serves as a Team Lead with Youthlinc, leading international humanitarian service teams in Thailand, Peru, Vietnam, Kenya, and Mongolia and mentoring participants throughout a year of local and international service. Her community involvement has also included leadership and volunteer work with Special Olympics, Habitat for Humanity, Make a Difference, and programs supporting women and children affected by domestic violence.

Across both her professional and volunteer work, Sandy is motivated by the opportunity to bring people together, build meaningful connections, and create experiences that make a lasting difference.

sections.title: About Shannon McRae
sections.html:
Shannon McRae has spent more than 27 years supporting executives and leadership teams, including more than 20 years with Utah Cancer Specialists. She began her career with UCS in 2004 as an HR Assistant and has since served in a variety of roles across the organization, supporting Human Resources, Clinical Services, Finance, executive leadership, and physicians. Most recently, she was promoted to Chief of Staff.

Throughout her career, Shannon has built a broad understanding of the organization and the people who make it successful. Her experience working alongside employees, nurse managers, finance leaders, physicians, and executives has given her a unique perspective on how each part of Utah Cancer Specialists contributes to the patient experience.

Shannon has always found fulfillment in caregiving and helping others. She originally came to UCS after a friend encouraged her to apply, and what began as a new job quickly became a place where she found purpose and a deep connection to the work.

She is especially passionate about helping the community understand better who Utah Cancer Specialists is, what the organization does, and why its work matters. She also believes strongly in creating an experience where patients feel connected to their care team and know they are heard, seen, and genuinely cared for.

Outside of work, Shannon enjoys trail running, spending time outdoors, traveling to be with family, supporting her children in their many activities, and occasionally finding time for a good nap.

sections.title: About Stephanie Waddoups
sections.html:
Stephanie has dedicated her career to caring for patients and supporting the teams who care for them. She has been with Utah Cancer Specialists for 13 years, serving as a nurse at Intermountain Medical Center and the Cancer Center, as well as Nurse Manager at Granger before moving into her current leadership role. Prior to joining UCS, Stephanie spent 16 years caring for newborns in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.

Stephanie earned her Bachelor of Science in Nursing from Brigham Young University and is a Registered Nurse and Oncology Certified Nurse (OCN).

She always knew she wanted to be a nurse and was drawn to the opportunity to care for others. Transitioning from newborn intensive care to oncology initially felt like a significant change, but she quickly found how meaningful it was to care for adults facing cancer. She has come to deeply value the relationships built with patients and families throughout their care.

Stephanie is especially excited about UCS’s continued commitment to putting patients first and expanding the ways the organization supports them. In addition to excellent cancer treatment, she values the growth of supportive services such as rehabilitation, supportive care, and mental health resources that address the needs of the whole patient.

For Stephanie, exceptional patient care is compassionate, individualized, and respectful. It means taking the time to truly listen, offering reassurance, and going above and beyond to make sure each patient feels cared for and supported.

Outside of work, Stephanie enjoys spending time with her family, especially skiing, fishing, and hiking. Of all her outdoor activities, skiing is her favorite.

sections.title: About Teresa Leavitt
sections.html:
Teresa Leavitt has built her career around healthcare, human resources, and supporting the people who care for patients. She began her professional journey working in physician offices and later served as Vice President of Volunteer and Talent Relations for Mountain West Ballet before joining Utah Cancer Specialists in 2007.

Teresa holds a bachelor’s degree in human resource management and has earned the PPMC designation through the American College of Medical Practice Executives. She is also an active member of both the national and local chapters of the Society for Human Resource Management.

Throughout her time at Utah Cancer Specialists, Teresa has especially enjoyed helping employees navigate onboarding, benefits, and the many day-to-day questions that come with being part of a growing organization. She has also played an important role in strengthening the UCS culture through employee events, recognition, and opportunities that help people feel connected and appreciated.

Having spent much of her HR career in healthcare, joining UCS felt like a natural return to work she knew and enjoyed. Teresa has always been drawn to the people side of healthcare and values knowing that, while she is not providing direct patient care, her work supports the employees who are.

What excites Teresa most about the future of Utah Cancer Specialists is seeing the organization continue to grow and evolve while remaining focused on the people it serves. Over the years, she has watched UCS expand its services, technology, and opportunities for both patients and employees, and she is proud to be part of an organization that continues to improve while staying true to its values.

Teresa believes exceptional patient care starts with exceptional people. From an HR perspective, that means making sure employees feel supported, valued, and equipped to do their best work so they can provide patients with the compassion, respect, and care they deserve.

Outside of work, Teresa enjoys spending time with family, reading, cooking, volunteering, and traveling.

sections.title: About Travis Gunther
sections.html:
With a background in molecular biology and healthcare leadership, Travis has spent much of his career helping advance diagnostic and treatment options for patients. He earned his bachelor’s degree in molecular biology from Brigham Young University and later completed his Master of Business Administration at the University of Utah.

Travis began his career at Myriad Genetics, where he performed BRCA genetic testing before moving into the company’s forensic laboratory. During that time, he contributed to efforts to identify victims of the September 11 attacks on the World Trade Center.

He later joined Utah Cancer Specialists as Laboratory Manager and was promoted to Director of Laboratory Services. In 2018, he expanded his leadership responsibilities to include UCS’s radiation and imaging services. Since then, he has helped grow the organization’s nuclear medicine program, including the development of UCS’s theragnostic program.

His interest in healthcare comes from a love of medicine and a desire to help people affected by cancer. He believes strongly in Utah Cancer Specialists’ vision and values the opportunity to help bring innovative treatments and technologies to patients in the community.

He is particularly excited about the continued advancement of theranostics and its potential to transform cancer care. Looking ahead, he hopes to help expand UCS’s involvement in Phase I–III clinical trials and provide patients greater access to emerging therapies.

Although his role does not involve daily patient interaction, he believes exceptional care begins with understanding each patient’s individual needs. For him, that means creating the best possible experience while ensuring patients have access to the latest and most effective treatment options available.

Outside of work, he enjoys spending time with his family and pursuing wildlife photography, a passion that combines his appreciation for the outdoors with creativity.

sections.title: About Tym Gilson
sections.html:
Tym Gilson brings more than 30 years of marketing experience across financial education, consumer products, professional services, and healthcare. He also has extensive experience in commercial real estate project management, overseeing projects ranging from restaurants and large warehouse facilities to medical and professional office spaces. Tym joined Utah Cancer Specialists in 2019 and has been closely involved in shaping both the organization’s growth and the experience it provides to patients, families, and staff.

His path to healthcare was driven by the challenge of creating a better experience for everyone impacted by cancer. Before joining UCS, Tym worked with several nonprofit organizations in California, including foundations focused on cancer awareness and support. Through that work, he encountered remarkable people and stories that reinforced his desire to help organizations better connect with and care for the communities they serve.

Tym is especially excited about the direction Utah Cancer Specialists is taking as healthcare becomes increasingly system driven. He believes UCS has an opportunity to do something different by preserving personal connections, remaining responsive to individual needs, and making the patient experience central to how the organization grows. Seeing long-term goals become reality and watching the UCS team turn opportunities for improvement into strengths has been particularly rewarding for him.

For Tym, exceptional patient care comes down to a simple question: Are we treating every patient the way we would want our own family to be treated? He believes the well-being of the people providing that care matters just as much. His work has included creating spaces specifically designed to support staff, recognizing that employees who feel cared for and supported are better equipped to provide exceptional experience for patients and families.

Outside of work, Tym is happiest spending time with his family and creating memories together. Faith, family, service, music, time on the water, and continually learning are important parts of his life. While he may claim free time is hard to find, he enjoys studying subjects that interest him and making the most of the time he has with the people who matter most.
